The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellants - original claimants, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 24.08.2006 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.) Mehsana, in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.510 of 2003, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,04,000/-
with 7.5% per annum interest to the claimant, holding the opponents i.e. driver, owner and insurance company liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text: On 18.04.2003, at about 12.00 hours, Pravinbhai was going on his bicycle from his service in Nirma Factory.

When he was trying to cross the road, opponent No.1 came there with his Tractor bearing Registration No.GJ- 08-B-5843 from Mahesana side, rashly and negligently, endangering human life and with excessive speed, and had dashed with the bicycle and accident has taken place.
In the result, Pravinbhai fall down on the road and received serious injuries and Pravinbhai succumbed to the injuries.
The Post-mortem was performed of the dead body of deceased Pravinbhai.
2.2. Notices were served to the opponents.
None were present except Opponents No.3 - insurance company.
Opponent No.3 - insurance company has filed its written statement at Exh.14 by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3. The Tribunal has framed the issues at Exh.19.
The NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the various documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal has been preferred by claimants before this Court for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Neeraj J. Vasu for the appellants - original claimants has submitted that the judgment and award passed by the learned tribunal is illegal unjust and against the provision of law and natural justice, the Tribunal has failed to appreciate that appellants have produced the salary slip of 14 days, which is of 1183 for 14 days and considering the salary slip, the Tribunal ought to have consider monthly income NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED:
13/06/2024 undefined of deceased to the tune of Rs.2535/- instead of Rs 2000/-, and the Tribunal ought to have considered future salary of the deceased to the tune of Rs.3800/- out of which entitlement of the petitioner i.e 1/3 of Rs 38,00/- would come to Rs.1265/- i.e Rs.15,192/- per annum and looking to the age of the petitioner no.2, the Tribunal ought to have given multiplier of 12 years that comes to Rs 1,82,304/-.
Furthermore, he has submitted that the Tribunal has also erred in awarding only Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate, love and affection.

The Tribunal ought to have held that deceased was only son of the appellants and now after the death of their son, there is no one to look after parents and appellants have to depend upon the paid servants to look after them and considering all this facts, the Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.25,000/- towards loss of estate love and affection.
Furthermore, the Tribunal has awarded the interest at the rate of 7.2% which is very less and ought to have awarded interest amount in to 12% per annum.
Hence, he has submitted that in view of the above referred premises, the quantum of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal is on a lower side against the well-establish principles of law.
Therefore, he has prayed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined to allow the present appeal by enhancing the amount of compensation.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati for the defendant No.3 - insurance company has jointly submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, as the Tribunal has considered all the aspects and passed the impugned judgment and award after considering the material available on the record.

However, from the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellants that the Tribunal has committed certain errors, on this aspect, learned advocates for the respondents have submitted that if this Court feels that there is some error in calculation of the amount in view of settled position of law, in awarding compensation by the Tribunal, then the Court may pass appropriate order by considering the submissions made by him, in the interest of justice.
Accordingly, he has submitted the calculation for the agreed amount.
6.1. I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
6.2. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.

6.3. 
For considering the facts of the case, I have considered the various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case, as under:
(i) National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680,
(ii) Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121,
(iii) Magma General Insurance Company Limited v.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, and (iv) New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Somwati and others, reported in 2020 (9) SCC 644.
6.4.

sentences.text: It appears from the records that the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,04,000/- at 7.5% per annum to the claimants.
It is undisputed that Pravinbhai, the deceased, died as a result of an accident caused by respondent No.1, the tractor driver.
The Tribunal has considered the deceased's income of Rs.84.50/- per day, amounting to Rs.2,520/- per month as per his pay-slip.
The age of the deceased, confirmed by a birth certificate on record, was 32 years at the time of the accident.
Despite documentary evidence, the Tribunal has presumed the deceased's monthly salary to be Rs.2,000/-.

The Tribunal has considered prospective income of the deceased of Rs.3,000/- per month and, taking into account that the deceased was unmarried and would have spent 2/3 of his Nathabhai Bababhai Makwana vs Kashiram Mafatlal Suthar on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164043772/

sentences.text: income on personal expenses, the Tribunal has calculated an annual loss of dependency at Rs.12,000/-.

Given the deceased's age and the ages of his parents (60 and 55 years), the Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined awarded multiplier of 7 only. Therefore, based on these considerations, the Tribunal awarded compensation to the claimants as follows:

6.5.

Considering the submissions and the aforementioned judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, the monthly income should be considered as Rs.2,197/-, in accordance with prevailing wages at that time, and this fact not disputed by the learned advocate for the respondent.
Based on the records, at the relevant time, the deceased was employed as a daily wage worker, indicating he was in service but not a permanent employee.
However, given the deceased's age, it could reasonably be assumed he NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined might have been appointed to a permanent position.

Therefore, taking this into account, an additional 50%
(Rs.1,099/-) as per the judgment in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra) is warranted, resulting in a total of Rs.3,296/-.
Furthermore, the Tribunal also erred in deducting 2/3 for personal expenses when it should have been 1/2, considering the deceased's earning status at the time of the accident.
Thus, after deducting 1/2, the amount comes to Rs.1,648/-.
Subsequently, applying a multiplier of 12 (12 months), the calculated amount is Rs.19,773/-.

Furthermore, considering the deceased's age of 32 at the time of the accident, multiplier of 16 should have been awarded as per the judgments in the cases of Pranay Shethi (supra) and Sarla Verma & Ors. (supra), instead of the multiplier of 7 awarded by the Tribunal.
Therefore, it comes to Rs.3,16,368/- for loss of income.

Furthermore, as both the claimants are parents, Rs.96,800/- (Rs.48,400/- each, calculated at Rs.40,000 x 10% x 10% each) should be awarded as per the judgment in the case of Somwati and others (supra).
Additionally, Rs.18,150/- should be considered for loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- for funeral expenses, totaling Rs.4,49,468/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4683/2008 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined 6.6.
